entry_json.avoid: 'Satisfied with', not 'satisfied about' or 'satisfied of'.

entry_json.definition: to make someone pleased by giving them what they want, or to meet a need or condition
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The explanation did not satisfy the residents who had complained.
example_sentences: Applicants must satisfy all three conditions.
A short walk does not satisfy the daily exercise guidelines.

contexts.text: The explanation did not satisfy the residents who had complained.
Applicants must satisfy all three conditions before an offer is made.
A short walk on its own doesn't really satisfy the daily exercise guidelines.

confusables.difference: Please is about making someone happy. Satisfy is about meeting a standard, need or condition.
Meet is the everyday alternative for requirements: 'meet the criteria'. Satisfy is slightly more formal.

entry_json.avoid: Change y to ie before -ed and -es: satisfied, satisfies.

entry_json.definition: an amount of money or resource that you do not have to spend or use, or money kept for the future
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Switching to LED lighting produced a saving of forty per cent.
example_sentences: She used her savings to pay for the course.
The changes will deliver significant savings over five years.

contexts.text: Switching to LED lighting produced a saving of roughly forty per cent on electricity.
I used most of my savings to pay for the course, which was worth it.
The proposed changes will deliver significant savings over a five-year period.

confusables.difference: In the plural, 'savings' means money kept in the bank. In the singular, 'a saving' is an amount not spent.
'An economy' in this sense means a reduction in spending, but is far less common than 'a saving'.

entry_json.avoid: 'A saving of £200', not 'a save of £200'. The noun from 'save' in this sense is 'saving'.

entry_json.definition: the size or extent of something, especially when it is large, or a range of levels used for measuring
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The scale of the housing shortage has been underestimated for years.
example_sentences: Damage on this scale takes decades to repair.
Responses were recorded on a scale of one to five.
collocations: on a scale of one to ten

contexts.text: The scale of the housing shortage has been consistently underestimated.
Damage on that scale takes decades and a lot of money to repair.
Responses were recorded on a scale of one to five, where five means strongly agree.

confusables.difference: Size is a measurement of one object. Scale is the extent of a whole situation or operation, and works with abstract nouns.
In British English 'scales' in the plural is the instrument for weighing things.

entry_json.avoid: 'On a large scale' takes 'on'. Do not write 'in a large scale'.

entry_json.definition: to look at something quickly to find particular information, or to use a machine to make a digital image
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Scan the passage for dates before you read it properly.
example_sentences: I scanned the document and emailed it.
Patients are scanned before and after treatment.

contexts.text: Scan the passage for dates and names before reading it in detail.
I scanned the form and emailed it, which saved a trip to the office.
Patients are scanned both before and after treatment to measure the change.

confusables.difference: Skimming is reading quickly for the general idea. Scanning is searching for one specific piece of information.
minimal_pair: skim the article for the argument
scan the timetable for your train

confusables.difference: Reading takes in everything; scanning deliberately ignores most of the text.

entry_json.avoid: Double the n: scanned, scanning.

entry_json.definition: an official plan or system designed to achieve something, especially one run by a government or organisation
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The recycling scheme has increased collection rates by a third.
example_sentences: A new scheme offers grants for home insulation.
The scheme was abandoned after two years.

contexts.text: The recycling scheme has increased collection rates by roughly a third.
There's a scheme in my city where you can borrow bikes for an hour free.
A new scheme offers grants of up to £5,000 for home insulation.

confusables.difference: A plan can be anyone's, including your own. A scheme is official, organised and usually open to the public to join.
In American English 'scheme' often suggests something dishonest. In British English it is neutral and very common in policy writing.

entry_json.avoid: Silent c: say SKEEM. In British English a scheme is not dishonest, so use it freely for policy in IELTS.

entry_json.definition: connected with science, or based on careful testing and evidence
entry_json.own_context_sentence: There is no scientific evidence to support the claim.
example_sentences: The article summarises recent scientific research on sleep.
A scientific approach requires you to test the idea, not just believe it.

contexts.text: There is currently no scientific evidence to support that particular claim.
I'm not scientific by nature; I trusted the doctor and that was that.
The article summarises recent scientific research on sleep and memory.

confusables.difference: Science is the noun, scientific the adjective. 'Science research' is not standard English.
Technical relates to practical methods and machinery; scientific relates to knowledge gained by testing.

entry_json.avoid: Stress the third syllable: sci-en-TIF-ic.

entry_json.definition: to give a loud high cry because you are frightened, hurt or excited
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Someone screamed when the lights went out.
example_sentences: The crowd screamed as the band came on stage.
She screamed for help but nobody heard.

contexts.text: Someone screamed when the lights suddenly went out.
The crowd screamed when the band came on, and I couldn't hear anything for hours.
Witnesses reported hearing a woman scream shortly before midnight.

confusables.difference: Shout is loud speech with words, often in anger. Scream is a high wordless cry of fear, pain or excitement.
Cry usually means weep. Scream is about volume and pitch, not tears.

entry_json.avoid: 'Scream at someone' means direct anger at them; 'scream for help' asks for rescue. The preposition changes the meaning.

entry_json.definition: the written text of a play, film or broadcast
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The script went through eleven drafts before filming began.
example_sentences: Actors receive the script several weeks in advance.
The dialogue in the script sounds nothing like real speech.

contexts.text: The script went through eleven separate drafts before filming began.
I wrote a short script for a student film once, which was harder than I expected.
Actors normally receive the script several weeks before rehearsals start.

confusables.difference: A scenario is a possible situation or outline of events. A script is the actual written dialogue.
The same word also means a writing system, as in 'Arabic script'.

entry_json.avoid: In IELTS Speaking, avoid sounding as if you are reading from a script. Memorised answers are penalised.

entry_json.definition: a work of art made by carving or shaping stone, wood or metal
entry_json.own_context_sentence: A large bronze sculpture stands at the entrance to the park.
example_sentences: The gallery specialises in modern sculpture.
She studied sculpture before turning to painting.

contexts.text: A large bronze sculpture stands at the entrance to the park.
There's a sculpture near my flat that I walk past every day and still like.
Public sculpture has been shown to increase how safe people feel in an area.

confusables.difference: A statue represents a person or animal realistically. A sculpture is any three-dimensional artwork, including abstract ones.
A sculptor is the artist; sculpture is the work.

entry_json.avoid: Uncountable as an art form ('she studies sculpture'), countable for individual works ('three sculptures').

entry_json.definition: less important than something else, or relating to the education of children aged about eleven to eighteen
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Cost was a secondary consideration when we chose the school.
example_sentences: She teaches history at a secondary school.
The secondary effects of the policy were not anticipated.

contexts.text: Cost was a secondary consideration when we chose the school.
I went to a secondary school about twenty minutes from my house.
Secondary education in the region is free but not compulsory beyond sixteen.

confusables.difference: Primary means most important, or for younger children. Secondary means less important, or for older children.
'High school' is American English. In IELTS, 'secondary school' is the safer British term.

entry_json.avoid: Do not write 'a secondary reason' when you mean an additional one. Secondary means less important, not simply extra.

entry_json.definition: safe from being harmed, lost or stolen, or certain to continue in the future
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Very few young workers now have a secure job.
example_sentences: Make sure the connection is secure before entering your details.
The building is secure and monitored at night.

contexts.text: Very few young workers now have what previous generations would call a secure job.
I don't feel secure in the flat because the front door doesn't lock properly.
Please check that the connection is secure before entering any payment details.

confusables.difference: Safe means free from danger right now. Secure means protected by something and likely to stay that way.
As a verb, secure means obtain something with effort: 'secure a place at university'.

entry_json.avoid: Stress the second syllable: si-KYOOR. As a verb it means 'obtain', which is a different meaning entirely.

entry_json.definition: protection against deliberate threats such as crime or attack, or the feeling of being safe
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Airport security has become far more time-consuming since 2001.
example_sentences: Job security matters more to some people than salary.
The building has security cameras at every entrance.

contexts.text: Airport security has become considerably more time-consuming since 2001.
Job security matters more to me than a higher salary, honestly.
The building has security cameras at every entrance and a staffed reception.

confusables.difference: Safety protects against accidents; security protects against deliberate harm such as theft or attack.
Security is the noun, secure the adjective. 'A security job' means working as a guard, not a stable job.

entry_json.avoid: 'Job security' means a stable job. 'A security job' means working as a security guard. Word order changes everything.

entry_json.definition: the small hard part of a plant from which a new plant grows
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Farmers who save their own seed are less dependent on suppliers.
example_sentences: Sunflower seeds are a cheap source of protein.
The seeds should be planted in early spring.

contexts.text: Farmers who save their own seed are much less dependent on commercial suppliers.
I planted some seeds on the balcony and, surprisingly, they grew.
The seeds should be planted in early spring and watered regularly.

confusables.difference: A pip is the small seed in fruit such as apples and oranges. Seed is the general word.
A plant is what grows; the seed is what it grows from.

entry_json.avoid: Seed is countable ('three seeds') but uncountable in farming ('save seed for next year').

entry_json.definition: to try to find or obtain something, or to try to do something
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Graduates seeking work in the sector face intense competition.
example_sentences: Patients should seek medical advice before stopping the treatment.
The company is seeking to reduce its energy use by half.

contexts.text: Graduates seeking work in the creative sector face intense competition.
Patients should seek medical advice before stopping any prescribed treatment.
Most people my age would seek advice online before asking anyone in person.

confusables.difference: Look for is the everyday phrasal verb. Seek is formal and belongs in writing, especially with advice, help and permission.
Search means examine a place thoroughly; seek means try to obtain something.

entry_json.avoid: Irregular past forms: sought, sought. Do not write 'seeked'.

entry_json.definition: to choose someone or something carefully from a group
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Participants were selected at random from the electoral register.
example_sentences: Only twelve applicants were selected for interview.
Select the option that best describes your situation.

contexts.text: Participants were selected at random from the electoral register.
Only twelve of us were selected for interview out of about two hundred.
Please select the option that best describes your current situation.

confusables.difference: Choose is the everyday word and can be casual. Select implies careful comparison against criteria and is standard in research writing.
Pick is informal and quick; select is deliberate and formal.

entry_json.avoid: Use 'choose' in Speaking. 'Select' can sound rehearsed in a natural conversation.

entry_json.definition: the process of choosing, or a group of things that have been chosen
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The selection process took almost three months.
example_sentences: The shop offers a wide selection of local produce.
Selection for the team is based entirely on performance.

contexts.text: The selection process took almost three months from application to offer.
There's a really good selection of restaurants near where I live.
Selection criteria should be published before applications open.

confusables.difference: A choice is the act or the freedom of choosing. A selection is the range available, or the formal process of choosing.
Range emphasises coverage from one extreme to the other; selection emphasises that someone has chosen what to offer.

entry_json.avoid: 'A wide selection of' is followed by a plural or uncountable noun, never a singular countable one.
